title: Magnetic phases of Kondo lattice materials Ce$_5$RhGe$_2$ and Ce$_5$IrGe$_2$
authors: Jiawen Zhang, Yanan Zhang, Mingyi Wang, Ye Chen, Yu Liu, Yongjun Zhang, Michael Smidman, Huiqiu Yuan
abstract: Single crystals of Ce$_5$RhGe$_2$ and Ce$_5$IrGe$_2$ have been systematically investigated by electrical resistivity, specific heat, and magnetization measurements. Together with Ce$_5$CoGe$_2$, all three compounds crystallize in the orthorhombic \emph{Pnma} structure, with the lattice parameters increasing monotonically from Co to Rh to Ir, consistent with the effect of negative chemical pressure. Magnetization measurements along the three principal crystallographic axes identify the \emph{a} axis as the easy magnetization direction throughout the series. Ce$_5$RhGe$_2$ exhibits ferromagnetic ordering with a Curie temperature of approximately 11.5 K and shows magnetic behavior closely resembling that of Ce$_5$CoGe$_2$. In contrast, Ce$_5$IrGe$_2$ undergoes two successive magnetic transitions at $T_{\rm M1}=12.7$ K and $T_{\rm M2}=11.8$ K, and there are multiple metamagnetic transitions under magnetic fields, giving rise to magnetization plateaus at fractions of the saturation magnetization $M_{\rm s}$ of approximately $M_{\rm s}/5$ and $M_{\rm s}/3$. The low-field metamagnetic transition along the easy axis shifts to lower field with decreasing temperature, and eventually a pronounced hysteresis loop is observed about zero-field, establishing that Ce$_5$IrGe$_2$ exhibits a ferrimagnetic ground state at the lowest measured temperatures.
summary: This paper experimentally investigates the magnetic phases in the Kondo lattice materials Ce5MGe2. By measuring transport and magnetic properties, the authors distinguish between ferromagnetic ordering in Ce5RhGe2 and a complex ferrimagnetic ground state in Ce5IrGe2. The work highlights how subtle changes in the transition metal element can drastically alter the magnetic ground state in these strongly correlated electron systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the magnetic phases and evolution of Kondo lattice materials, specifically Ce5RhGe2 and Ce5IrGe2, to understand the interplay between magnetism and electronic properties.
main_result: Ce5RhGe2 exhibits ferromagnetic ordering, while Ce5IrGe2 displays complex behavior, including two successive magnetic transitions and a ferrimagnetic ground state at low temperatures.
method: The research employed systematic measurements on single crystals, including electrical resistivity, specific heat, magnetization, and magnetic susceptibility, across varying temperatures and magnetic fields.
model_or_system: The physical system is the series of Kondo lattice compounds Ce5MGe2 (M = Co, Rh, Ir), which crystallize in the orthorhombic Pnma structure.
key_observables: Curie temperature (Tc), magnetic transition temperatures (TM1, TM2), magnetization plateaus (e.g., Ms/5, Ms/3), and the electronic specific heat coefficient (gamma0).
important_parameters: Temperature (T), applied magnetic field (H), and the chemical substitution element (M = Co, Rh, Ir).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed magnetic transitions and electronic properties are governed by the competition between local moments and conduction electrons.
figures_summary: Figures show resistivity, specific heat, and magnetization measurements across the series, illustrating magnetic transitions and field-dependent plateaus.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares the structural and magnetic properties of Ce5MGe2, detailing the magnetic transitions observed in each compound, particularly contrasting the FM behavior of Ce5RhGe2 with the complex FIM-like state of Ce5IrGe2.
why_interesting: The study provides detailed experimental evidence of magnetic ground states (FM vs. FIM) in heavy fermion systems, which are canonical examples of strongly correlated electron physics, relevant for understanding exotic quantum phases.
